'''''Kyselo''''' or '''''krkonošské kyselo''''' is a traditional Bohemian sour soup featuring mushrooms and [[w:sourdough|sourdough]]. It originates from the [[w:Krkonoše|Krkonoše]] mountain region in northern [[w:Bohemia|Bohemia]]. Kyselo is a nutritious food, so it is often served as a main course, but in small quantities it could also be served as a soup course.

==Ingredients==

* [[Cookbook:Potato|Potatoes]]
* 100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Sourdough Starter|sourdough]] starter, ideally made with [[Cookbook:Rye|rye]] flour
* 15 g dried [[Cookbook:Porcini Mushroom|porcini mushrooms]], preferably Central European
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Caraway|caraway seeds]]
* 1250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 20 g [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 3 chicken [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Vinegar|Vinegar]]
* Chopped green [[Cookbook:Spices and Herbs|herbs]], such as [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] or [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallion]]

== Equipment ==
* Stockpots
* Bowls
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Frying pan]]
* Mixing spoon

==Procedure==

# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] potatoes with their skins, then peel them, chop onto small pieces and [[w:roast|roast]] it in a pan (without adding grease). 
# Put 250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] tepid water into a bowl. Stir in the sourdough starter. Cover with a clean cloth, and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes to 3 hours.
# Put 1000 ml water into a stockpot. Add the dried mushrooms and caraway, and boil for at least 15 minutes to make a strong [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]].
# Carefully add the sourdough mixture into the broth, stirring well—there is a danger that the sourdough will shrink into small dumplings.
# Boil the soup, stirring, until the sourdough thickens the mixture. This should take about 10 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the chopped onion with butter in a pan. Stir it into the soup.
# Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, and scramble them in an ungreased pan. Stir the cooked eggs into the soup.
# Season the soup to taste with salt and vinegar. It should be mildly sour, flavored primarily by the mushrooms and sourdough.
# Served the soup hot, garnished with the chopped herbs, with the potatoes as a side dish. Individual diners may wish to add additional vinegar and salt to taste.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

=== Variations ===
* The eggs can also be be [[Cookbook:Hard Cooked Eggs|hard-boiled]] and chopped instead of scrambled.
* Sometimes kyselo is made softer by adding [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]].
* 150 g fresh mushrooms may be used instead of the dried ones.
* The potatoes are sometimes boiled directly in the water: added at beginning into the stockpot and then logically not roasted. But, roasted potatoes are crispy and more delicious. There are also variants without potatoes.

=== Notes ===
* Do not the potatoes to the soup; potatoes should be served separately and added by consumer itself just before eating. It preserves the crispness of the potatoes.
* Sometimes other sour, mushroom-based [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Czechia|Czech]] soups are mistakenly referred to as ''kyselo''. The difference is that ''kulajda'' and other such similar soups use sour cream or milk and vinegar instead of sourdough. To avoid confusion, kyselo is often called ''Krkonošské kyselo'', meaning "kyselo from the Krkonoše region".
* Kyselo is closely related to a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Poland|Polish]] sour rye soup called ''Żurek'' or ''Żur'', which contains meat and no mushrooms.
* [[Cookbook:Sourdough Starter|Sourdough starter]] can be bought at local food stores in Krkonoše. Elsewhere, it can be purchased at specialty shops and local bakeries. It can also be made at home from water and flour.

==External links==
* [http://dadalovakucharka.cz/pol/polr0137.html Another kyselo recipe with handy information how to make sourdough.] But unfortunately in Czech language
* [http://multi.xeres.cz/jidlo/prave-krkonoske-kyselo Strictly traditional kyselo.] But unfortunately in Czech language.
